app_layer.summary: All /api/admin/* establishment writes use fixed hardcoded payloads via service-role client (never forward request-body fields). /api/claims only creates establishment_claims rows, never writes establishments directly. owner_id is only ever set by /api/admin/claims/[id]/approve. No app-layer escalation path found (same conclusion as REGISTRY-NATIONAL-D, files unchanged this sprint).

rls_layer.evidence: reports/registry/registry-national-d1-owner-write-reproduction.json — a real authenticated owner session wrote to all 5 tested registry-protected columns on their own row, bypassing the app entirely via direct Supabase REST.
rls_layer.owner_can_edit_official_verification: Indirectly YES — official_verification in resolveEstablishmentTrustState() reads official_id/source_ministry (for OFFICIAL_SOURCE_FOUND) which the owner can currently fabricate; OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED itself still requires a establishment_registry_identifiers row with CORROBORATED/CONFIRMED status, which remains correctly unreachable by the owner (identifier table confirmed secure, registry-national-d1-identifier-table-security.json). So an owner CANNOT reach OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED, but CAN currently fabricate OFFICIAL_SOURCE_FOUND by writing source_ministry themselves.
rls_layer.owner_can_edit_registry_identifiers_tabl: NO (live-confirmed secure, separate table, RLS blocks all non-service-role writes)

overall: Real escalation path confirmed live at the RLS layer for establishments' 6 registry-provenance columns. Fix: execute 0023 (audited this sprint, decision A — ready as-is).
